decisive_items: Clinical Exome Sequencing detected a pathogenic nonsense variant in the CHD2 gene [NM_001271.4:c.5035C>T p.(Arg1679Ter)]
weekly recurrent episodes of fixed gaze, absence-like loss of contact, and myoclonic-like movements of upper and lower arms lasting from a few seconds to 15 minutes, with frequent falls
Family history includes mother with moderate intellectual disability and childhood-onset epilepsy, maternal grandmother with late-onset epilepsy, and maternal aunt with mild intellectual impairment
response.rationale: Pathogenic CHD2 variant with epilepsy, developmental delay, and relevant family history is definitive for CHD2-related epilepsy; R5 describes the seizure phenotype but not the underlying diagnosis, while other candidates are unsupported or based on an incidental inherited cytogenetic finding.

rejected.why: The inherited inv(16) is a cytogenetic finding but not established as the cause of this phenotype; CHD2 pathogenic variant is the definitive diagnosis.
No evidence of mosaic variegated aneuploidy; the inversion alone does not support this diagnosis.
Facial features are nonspecific and no TCF4 variant or other Pitt-Hopkins hallmark is present.
Intellectual disability is a feature of the presentation but not the specific syndromic diagnosis.
